lens: F6_Better_Alternative — What other approaches were possible? Why not those? If 'later', is there a bounded FixupTask? Did the author consider Linus-style and hyperscaler-style alternatives?
answer: PASS_WITH_RESERVATIONS. ADR-0118 explicitly enumerates three rejected alternatives (keep-empty-active, rename-into-M-CC-P11 gate, delete-all-mentions) with one-line rationales — that is a real F6-compliant alternatives ledger, not hand-waving. Retirement-over-deprecation is defensible because the invariant is one-time (pre-grit cutover boundary), so an ADR-0108 sunset window would only delay deletion of code whose inputs no longer exist. However, the same-day Accepted→Retired bypass of ADR-0108 (landed 2026-05-15, one day before PR #13 on 2026-05-16) is NOT explicitly justified in ADR-0118; readers must infer 'one-time lane needs no sunset window' rather than read it. The bundle-vs-split choice (retirement + ADR-0104/0107 amendments + IP-008 evidence in one 24-file PR) is correct for atomicity (no half-retired references in living docs) but is not defended in the PR body. The tombstone-lane alternative (always-pass with 'retired' message) is rejected implicitly via 'keep-empty-active' — that mapping should be made explicit.
key_claims: ADR-0118 §Rejected alternatives names three competing options with reasoning — exceeds the F6 minimum of 'one Linus + one hyperscaler alternative'.

Retirement-vs-deprecation: correctly chosen because the invariant gates a one-time cutover boundary (pre-grit-cutover-2026-05-12 payload removal); a sunset window cannot produce new violations after the payload itself is deleted in the same PR.
ADR-0108 sunset-lifecycle bypass is defensible on substance (one-time lane, no consumers post-cutover) but undocumented in ADR-0118 — a 2-line 'why no sunset window' paragraph would close the gap.

Bundle-vs-split: 24 files in one PR is correct because separating ADR-0104/0107 amendments from the kernel/app deletion would leave dangling references to the retired crate name in living ADRs during the gap window.

Tombstone-lane alternative (always-pass with explicit 'retired' message) is rejected implicitly via the 'keep the lane active with an empty archive set → false mechanical confidence' rationale — should be named explicitly so future retirements cite the precedent.

Migrate-coverage-to-other-lane is implicitly handled by naming `oya-foundry-fitness-adapter-with-no-importer-kernel` as the landed mechanical-prevention sibling in the ADR-0104 amendment — that IS the migration story, but ADR-0118 does not cite it under 'Rejected alternatives'.

Historical lane docs preserved at docs/fitness-lanes/archive-orphan.md and .omc/fitness-lanes/archive-orphan.md with retired_by/retired_on frontmatter is the correct hyperscaler-style choice (tombstone the metadata, delete the executable) — analogous to AWS service-deprecation pages.
uncertainty_areas: Whether ADR-0108 sunset-lifecycle policy text itself carves out 'one-time lanes' as exempt — if yes, PR #13 is in-policy; if no, this is a precedent-setting exception that should be flagged in the sunset-lifecycle ADR.
Whether the registry/catalog deletions (3 yaml files) trigger any downstream consumer that expected the capability — no consumer audit appears in the PR body.
Whether ADR-0052 (superseded by ADR-0118) needs a superseded_by frontmatter update in a follow-up PR — diff does not show ADR-0052 being touched.
alternatives_considered: A: Hard retire + remove executable + keep historical lane docs (THE SELECTED PATH — landed in PR #13, captured in ADR-0118).
B: Deprecate-with-sunset-window per ADR-0108 — mark lane Deprecated for N days, then remove. Rejected by substance (one-time invariant, payload already gone) but not by inline ADR-0118 reasoning.

C: Migrate-coverage-to-other-lane — fold archive-payload-presence check into authoritative-tracked or adapter-with-no-importer lane. Implicitly handled (sibling lane named in ADR-0104 amendment) but not cited as a 'considered alternative' in ADR-0118.

D: Convert-to-tombstone lane — keep crate, always emit Pass with `status: retired, replacement: M-CC-P11` payload. Rejected as 'false mechanical confidence' (good rationale) but the tombstone variant is not distinguished from the empty-set variant in ADR-0118.

E: Bundle vs split into 3 PRs (retirement + ADR amendments + IP-008 evidence). Bundle selected for atomicity (no dangling references in living docs during gap window) but rationale is absent from PR body.

F: Rename-into-M-CC-P11 gate — wrap archive-orphan kernel as an M-CC-P11 admission primitive. Rejected because projected-merge-state + conflict-kernel already own the replacement invariant — correctly named in ADR-0118.
selected_rationale: Option A (hard retire + tombstoned docs + bundled PR) is correct because: (1) the invariant is one-time, so a sunset window cannot produce new violations after the payload is deleted in the same PR — making ADR-0108 substantively N/A; (2) bundling the ADR-0104/0107 amendments with the crate deletion prevents dangling references to the retired crate name in living docs; (3) the kept lane metadata files (docs/fitness-lanes/archive-orphan.md, .omc/fitness-lanes/archive-orphan.md) with retired_by/retired_on frontmatter are the hyperscaler-style tombstone — analogous to AWS service-deprecation pages; (4) ADR-0118 supersedes ADR-0052 explicitly, preserving traceability; (5) the migration story IS captured (adapter-with-no-importer-kernel as the landed sibling) just not under 'Rejected alternatives'.
rejected_reasons: B (Deprecate-with-sunset per ADR-0108): SUBSTANTIVELY correct rejection — a one-time invariant whose payload is removed in the same PR has no 'new violation' surface during a sunset window. But the rejection is NOT named in ADR-0118; readers must infer it. FOLLOWUP: add a 2-line 'Why no sunset window' paragraph citing 'one-time invariant, payload removed in same ChangeSet'.

C (Migrate-coverage): partial migration DID happen (adapter-with-no-importer-kernel cited in ADR-0104 amendment) — the rejection is really 'no migration needed for the original invariant, sibling lane covers the residual concern'. Should be named explicitly so the precedent is reusable.

D (Tombstone-lane always-pass): correctly rejected as false mechanical confidence — an always-pass lane is worse than no lane because it consumes CI budget and produces misleading green signal. But the tombstone variant should be distinguished from the empty-set variant in ADR-0118 to make the precedent reusable for future retirements.
E (Split into 3 PRs): correctly rejected for atomicity but not documented in PR body. Splitting would create gap windows where living ADRs reference deleted crates.

F (Rename into M-CC-P11 gate): CORRECTLY rejected and CORRECTLY named in ADR-0118 — projected-merge-state and conflict-kernel already own the replacement invariant, so a rename would create overlapping coverage.
linus_style_alternative: Single-commit hard delete — no ADR, no tombstoned lane docs, just `rm -rf` the dead crates and amend Cargo.toml. Cost: lost traceability for IP-008 evidence. Benefit: minimal diff, no ceremony. Correctly rejected by the as-shipped path because ADR-0052 and IP-008 evidence need a forwarding pointer (ADR-0118) for future archaeologists to understand why the archive-orphan crate name appears in older ADRs. The kept lane-docs-as-tombstone IS the Linus-style 'good taste' choice: preserve enough metadata to explain history, delete enough to prevent the dead code from being mistaken for live infrastructure.
hyperscaler_style_alternative: Soft-retire via lifecycle automation per ADR-0108: mark crate `[package.metadata.oya.sunset]` with retired_on=2026-05-16 + removal_date=2026-08-16, let the sunset-lifecycle kernel emit deprecation warnings for 90 days, then auto-remove on schedule. Cost: 90 days of dead code in the workspace + sunset-lifecycle lane warnings on every CI run. Benefit: zero-touch retirement, downstream consumer detection during the window. Rejected substantively because (a) there are no downstream consumers — the crate's only inputs (pre-grit archive payload) are removed in the same PR; (b) the invariant is one-time, not a contract whose consumers need migration time; (c) the sunset-lifecycle lane itself only landed 2026-05-15, so there is no operational pattern yet for retiring crates that were already known-dead. FOLLOWUP: ADR-0108 should explicitly carve out 'one-time invariant lanes whose inputs are removed in the same ChangeSet' as exempt from the sunset window, citing PR #13 as the precedent.
